Why RainSMP

Built for the long game.

Everything here is designed to outlast a single weekend — a world worth coming back to.

Persistent world

No resets between seasons. Terrain, farms, and builds carry forward permanently.

Land

No griefing is allowed in the server, no exceptions.

Player economy

Trade at the market, run a shop, or work the weekly auction house.

Weekly events

Storm Nights, boss raids, and build contests, every week without fail.

Server Rules

Short version: don't ruin it for everyone else. Full list below.

01

Respect

  1. No meanness, harassment, hate speech, or discrimination. Be decent to other players.
  2. English is the primary language in global chat, for moderation purposes.
  3. No spamming, chat flooding, or excessive caps.
02

No claims, no excuses

  1. This server has no land claim or chunk protection plugin — everything is built on trust.
  2. No stealing from chests, farms, or storage that isn't yours.
  3. No griefing: don't break, burn, flood, or edit builds that aren't yours.
  4. Traps designed purely to steal, grief, or ruin someone's base are not allowed.
03

Economy

  1. Duplication glitches must be reported, not used. Exploiting them is a permanent ban.
  2. Real-money trading for in-game currency or items is not allowed.
  3. Shops must list prices clearly. Scamming other players results in an economy ban.
04

Fair play

  1. No cheat clients, X-ray, or unfair advantage mods.
  2. Advertising other servers in chat is not allowed.
  3. Staff decisions are final. Appeals go through the Discord ticket system.

Wiki / Fishing

Fishing

Fish can be caught with a fishing rod or a crab trap in any water or lava source, whether it was placed by a player or generated naturally. What bites depends on where your bobber sits and the conditions at that moment.

Where

Biome & water type

Ocean, river and freshwater each have their own pool. In the Nether the fish depend on the biome.

When

Time of day

Fish are marked day, night or any time, so some only bite after dark.

Season

Spring to winter

The pool changes every season. Many fish only appear in one or two.

Weather

Clear or rain

Some fish need clear skies and others only show up in rain or snow.

Wiki / Skills / Overview

Skills

Skills are activities you level up through play. Each skill has 12 levels. Every level fills an XP bar and awards a point to spend in the Skills Panel (K by default). At levels 5, 8 and 12 your path splits in two. The path you skip is locked unless you use a Crystal of Regret to reset. Every skill has at least one level 12 node that gives a way to get Prismatic Shards.

Farming

Harvesting crops, collecting from Artisan Machines and eating prepared food.

Wiki / Farming / Basics

Farming

Crops come from seeds and fruit trees and are used for money, cooking, quests and artisan goods. Farming is simple once you know the daily rhythm.

Till

Use a hoe on dirt to make farmland, then right-click seeds onto it. Planted crops do not drop seeds when broken.

Hydrate

Nearby water does not hydrate farmland. Use watering cans, sprinklers, rain, water bottles or splash potions. Dry farmland can turn to dirt and destroy the crop.

Seasons

Most crops only grow in certain seasons. Wrong-season crops stay planted but do not grow. Some biomes, like Taiga, are a permanent season.

Fertilize

Right-click farmland with fertilizer for faster growth, better quality, hydration or more yield. A pitchfork has a 50% chance to recover it.

Growth

At 6:00 AM, watered crops in season grow one stage. At 100% right-click to harvest. Diamond, Netherite and Neptunium hoes harvest several at once.

Quality

Normal, Silver, Gold or Iridium. Better fertilizer and seeds from the Seed Maker raise quality. Iridium needs Pristine Quality Fertilizer.

Sprinkler layout

Tap to zoom

Sprinklers can sit above or level with farmland, so staggered farms work.

Wiki / Farming / Fruit Trees

Fruit Trees

Fruits can be harvested from fruit trees and animals. They are mainly used for money, cooking, quests and artisan goods. Plant a sapling, wait for the right season and come back to pick.

Plant

Saplings

Right-click a dirt block with a sapling to plant the matching tree.

Grow

Tree growth

Trees only grow during their own season, and the time it takes is random. Tree Fertilizer speeds them up.

Harvest

Picking fruit

Right-click the fruit to harvest it, or let a Drum of the Cornucopia do it automatically.

Season

Harvest windows

Fruit can only be picked in its season, and the time it takes to ripen is random too.

Tips

  • Two kinds of sapling. Apples and cherries come as a plain sapling (seasonal, bigger yield) and as a tree sapling (dark cherry for cherries). The tree versions keep growing year-round but yield less per harvest.
  • Skill perks. Each fruit harvest gives 30 Farming XP, and Tree Whisperer (Farming level 8) adds +2 fruit when you harvest by hand. Extra fruit gives no bonus XP.
  • Banana Karenina. This skill book doubles Banana Tree output. It has a 0.1% chance to drop from a Banana Tree.
  • Prismatic Shard saplings. Lemon, Hazenut, Pawpaw and Cinnamon saplings can be bought with prismatic shards from the Baker, so save your shards from level 12 skill nodes.

Wiki / Reference / Skill Books

Skill Books

Skill Books give you special abilities when read. Most are rare drops tied to the task they help with, so the best way to find one is to keep doing that task.

How to get them

  • Do the task the book is about and wait for the drop chance (see the Source column).
  • Buy from the Wandering Trader, who rolls 2 books out of all possible books each time they spawn.
  • Buy from the Bookseller, who appears on the phone in the Late Season.
  • Each season has 2 unique books for sale that can only be bought in that season.
  • Win one from the Prize Machine.

Wiki / Husbandry / Animals

Animals

Animals are one of the central farming mechanics. They need more up front and more upkeep than crops, but they pay far better. Any animal you obtain, by any method, can be farmed as long as it is a valid husbandry animal.

Stat

Affection

A semi-permanent stat of how familiar the animal is with you. It affects the quality of every output.

Stat

Mood

A temporary stat worked out the first time you interact with an animal each day.

Drops

Foraging

Animals drop rare items as their affection climbs. Jump to the table below.

Affection

Affection has a maximum of 1,000, and every 100 is one full heart in the animal UI. Certain forages also have affection requirements.

Max 1,000One heart 100

Gained by

  • Petting
  • Milking
  • Hand-feeding
  • Eating certain feeds, like Candied Animal Feed and Mana Feed
  • Level 5 Husbandry skills

Lost by

  • Cramped living conditions
  • Using Magic Shears
  • Going longer than a day without feeding

Mood has a maximum of 256 and shows up as smiles and frowns in the animal UI. You can check the full calculation with the Mood Scanner. A Sunlit Crystal skips mood completely by permanently putting the animal in a good mood, whatever its conditions.

At mood 160 or higher an animal can produce quality items, as long as its affection is high enough.

Artisan Goods

Artisan goods are items made in artisan machines. A machine takes one or more raw materials and, after a day or a few, turns them into something worth a lot more.

How it works

Insert, wait, collect

Put raw materials in and the machine runs for one or more days. Output quality usually follows the lowest-quality item you put in.

Jade panel

A green exclamation mark floats above a machine when its product is ready to collect.

Wiki / Slimes / Care

Feeding, Largos and Happiness

Each breed has a specific diet, shown in the Jade panel when you hover over it. Slimes eat a dropped item, a living mob, or food from a Slime Feeder.

Slime categories

Pure

Pure Slimes

The basic slime from a Slime Incubator, with only one breed. Max size 3. Feed one a Plort of another breed and it becomes a Largo.

Largo

Largo Slimes

Made when a Pure Slime eats another breed's Plort. Max size 4. They inherit the diet, favorite food and Plorts of both breeds, so they are the best for farming.

Danger

Tarr

A Largo that eats a third kind of Plort becomes a Tarr. Tarrs eat Largos, Pure Slimes and players, grow after each meal and turn eaten slimes into Tarrs. Keep your pen tidy.

When a slime eats

  • Below its max size (3 for Pure slimes), the slime grows.
  • It is healed by 1 heart.
  • At size 3 or more, it produces a Plort of its breed. A Largo also produces a Plort of its sub-breed.
  • It gets happier, and its happiness stops dropping if it was starving.
  • If it eats its favorite food (as an item, a mob, or both), it produces an additional Plort for each breed.

Experiment with a slime's diet and work out its favorite foods.

Happiness

Every slime has a happiness value that rises or falls with what happens to it. A newly spawned slime starts at half of the maximum. The happiness system is still a work in progress and will be expanded.

Goes up when

  • It feeds. Its favorite food doubles the increase.
  • It feeds near at least 3 slimes of the same breed (Largos count) for a small boost, or near 6 to 7 for a bigger one.
  • It eats Slime Candy, which moves it up to the next happiness stage (for example sad to neutral).

Goes down when

  • It is starving, which lowers happiness gradually.
  • It is killed, which greatly lowers happiness.
  • It feeds while crowded (near 9 or more slimes of the same breed), which greatly lowers happiness.

Happiness states

Best

Happy

Performs its positive behaviors, more often the happier it is.

Default

Neutral

No negative behaviors and no positive ones. Incubated slimes are born in this state.

Low

Sad

Still produces Plorts, but performs negative behaviors more and more as happiness drops.

Danger

Furious

Attacks the player, often performs negative behaviors, makes no Plorts and will not turn into a Largo.

Wiki / Slimes / Traits

Slime Traits

Traits are custom behaviors a breed can have. A slime can have any number of traits, or none. Largo Slimes have the traits of both breeds they contain.

Hazard

TraitEffect
ExplosiveWhen hungry, the slime periodically causes explosions that do not break blocks. They get more frequent as hunger grows.
NuclearWhen furious, the slime bursts apart in a high-powered explosion that breaks blocks.
FeralAlways attacks the player.
FlamingSets mobs it touches on fire. When hungry, it periodically creates fire, more often as hunger grows.
SpikyHurts the player on touch.
InverseFlips behaviors: good effects happen when the slime is unhappy, and bad ones happen when it is sad.
PutridIncreases the strength of effects and doubles their duration.
WeepingPeriodically cries and fills the area with water. If there is not enough space for its tears, it gets sadder.

Diet

TraitEffect
PickyA slime made into a Largo gets angry if it eats from the same diet twice in a row.
LargolessCannot be made into a Largo, and its Plorts cannot make other slimes into Largos.
FoodportingTeleports to the food items and entities it targets.
DominantSlimes of this breed only eat from its diet when turned into a Largo.
RecessiveSlimes of this breed never eat from its diet when turned into a Largo.

Living conditions

TraitEffect
AquaticSinks in water and gets unhappy when not in it.

DiverseGets upset if it is not close to 3 unique breeds that are not its own.

Wiki / Getting Started / Getting Started

Getting Started

The first thing to do after spawning is forage for sellable goods and find a good spot for a home. Everything below is a quick path through your first days.

Sell

Shipping Bin

Anything with a coin amount in its tooltip is sellable. Put it in a Shipping Bin and it sells at 6am every morning.

Forage

Early money

Pumpkins, berry bushes and bales of crops give a good starting cash boost. Chests hold food, experience books and equipment.

Quests

Quest book

Follow the Getting Started quests to learn tool and weapon upgrades. They also award a Farm House you can place without building.

Settle

Pick a biome

Beach and savanna biomes are permanent summer, which makes them a good place to start a farm.

Farming

Water

Every morning

Water crops with a Watering Can after 6am. Dry farmland can turn to dirt and break the crop. Sprinklers hydrate nearby farmland at 6am instead.

Harvest

Right-click

Harvesting keeps the seed in the ground. A seed pouch plants a 3x3 when shifting. Diamond hoes and above harvest 5x5, lower hoes 3x3.

Process

Add value

Processing raises value. Two tomatoes make tomato sauce in the cooking pot. Pumpkin bread, dumplings and jams are good early recipes.

Mining and the Nether

Overworld

Ores and geodes

Find vanilla ores and zinc. Earth crystals are used in many artisan machine recipes, the cooking pot and the cutting board. Geodes can drop aquamarine, which makes crab traps.

Crab traps

Rare goodies

Crab traps fish up items like slime hearts and neptunium nuggets.

Nether

Flint and steel

Buy flint and steel from the Blacksmith, since it cannot be crafted. The Nether has raw bismuth ore, fire crystals, bastions and fortresses. Bastions can hold coins worth 32K.

Batteries

Charging Rods

Blaze rods make Charging Rods. When struck by lightning they drop a battery after 4 days. Batteries power advanced and automated machines.

Skills. Doing activities earns skill XP. Each level gives a point to spend with K by default. Higher levels change how you farm, so plan around them. Everything can be automated.

Wiki / Create / Create Recipes

Create Recipes

The modpack changes many Create recipes to fit the economy. These are the differences from regular Create.

Late game

Drill, Saw, Harvester

These now need late game materials like Iridium or Netherite, Prismatic Shards and Ancient Coins, which take a good income flow.

Copper

Treated Logs

Copper Casings now require Treated Logs instead of regular Stripped Logs.

Power

Kinetic Blueprints

Needed for Create power sources. Unlocked by finishing the Boiler Room Bundle, can be duplicated, and the Witch sells a replacement.

Wiki / World / Longwings

Longwings

Longwings is the modpack term for butterflies and moths. They are Adventurer Products and can be sold, with a price based on rarity and size.

Price (16 - rarity) x 78 + size bonusSize bonus Size / 0.01 x 4Sizes Small 0.75, Normal 0.95, Larger 1.0
Metamorphosize book. This skill book triples the size bonus. At size 1.0 it adds 800 to the price.

Drops and breeding

Amber and pollen

Every 5 minutes

Butterflies drop Butterfly Amber and moths drop Moth Pollen. Chance = unique nearby flowers x 0.15 minus nearby longwings x 0.1, capped at 100%.

Eggs

A quarter of the chance

Caterpillar Eggs use the same rules at a quarter of the chance. Parents are the nearest longwings when the egg spawns. Hatch eggs in a Caterpillar Box or sell them.

Species

Cross-breeding

Both parents decide the species, so cross-breeding can reveal new species without lures.

Size

Average of parents

Egg size is the average of both parents. The hatchling keeps it if it is under double the breed max size.

Getting rarer longwings

Offspring can only be one tier rarer than the rarest parent (lower number is rarer). 1) Breed two tier 5s to get a tier 4. 2) Breed that tier 4 with any longwing to get a tier 3. 3) Always keep your rarest longwing as a parent.

Wiki / World / Seasons

Seasons

Sunlit Valley has four seasons of 30 days. Each season has three sub-seasons (early, mid and late) lasting 10 days each. The world follows one global cycle that does not depend on biome.

Spring Summer Autumn Winter
Crops

Local season

Most crops only grow in the local season shown on the seed tooltip or in the Farmer's Almanac. Greenhouse Glass bypasses this.

Fish

Global season

Fish only bite in the season on their tooltip, based on the world's global season. A Fish Finder book lists them.

Charging Rods

Winter

Charging Rods do not work in Winter unless upgraded with a Frosted Tip.

Mobs

Late Autumn / Winter

Zombies and Skeletons can spawn as trick-or-treaters in Late Autumn and frozen in Late Winter.

Statues

Rotating trades

Ancient Goddess Statue trades rotate every season.

Shops

Seasonal stock

The Bookseller sells 2-3 season-exclusive books and the Carpenter sells sub-season wallpapers.

Biomes and seasons

Biomes only change the season for crops. Only Summer and Winter have exclusive biomes. Tropical biomes count as Summer and show a Wet or Dry season in the top-left UI. Outside of rain in the wet season, the difference is only how foliage looks.

Always Summer (tropical)

Wiki / Mods / Cozy Cafes

Cozy Cafes

A cafe is run by a Cafe Manager. Serve drinks, mains and desserts to customers, earn reputation stars and grow your cafe.

Opening a cafe

Menu

3+ items

At least 3 items on the menu (3 per star by default).

Block

Cafe Menu

At least one Cafe Menu block in the working area.

Block

Cafe Sign

A linked Cafe Sign block for customers to spawn. It can be outside the working area.

Space

No other managers

No other open Cafe Managers within a 9x9x9 area around the manager. It can open once per Minecraft day.

Menu items

Drinks

Served first

Every customer orders a drink if one is on the menu. Empty bottles drop on the floor afterwards.

Mains

Highest price

Mains earn the most reputation. Mains without a bowl need a Serving Plate from a Plating Station. Dirty dishes must be cleared before a new customer sits.

Desserts

50% chance

Customers order dessert 50% of the time by default, unless the menu is only desserts. No plates needed.

Dishes

Wash them

Hold right click on a sponge block or a modded sink. Controlled by the tag #cozycafe:cleans_dishes.

Reputation (stars)

Each star is 1000 reputation. Stars decide how many menu items you need, how big your cafe is and how many customers spawn each day.
Dish typeReputation
Drink2

Dessert4

Based on the max wait time, 50 seconds by default.

Quality bonus

With the quality food mod. Added before service multipliers.

Camera

Load a film, look through the viewfinder, compose your shot and release the shutter. The camera comes from the Exposure mod.

Tap to zoom

Overview of the camera, attachments and camera stand.

Attachments

Tap to zoom
AttachmentUsed for
FilmRequired to take photos
FilterGlass Panes

LensSpyglass

Viewfinder controls

Tap to zoom

Hold sneak or the middle mouse button to show the controls. Zooming is slower and more precise while they are shown.

ControlWhat it does

Wiki / Mods / Camera Stand

Camera Stand

The camera stand is an entity that holds a camera to take photos remotely.

Tap to zoom
Place

Use with a camera

Interact with the stand while holding a camera to place it. Interact with the camera on the stand to position it.

Attachments

Sneak + use

Sneak and interact to open the attachments menu or swap an attachment.

Remove

Hit it

Hitting the stand pops the camera off. Hitting again breaks the stand.

Self-timer

Photograph yourself

Take photos of yourself from a distance. Selfie mode is not available.

Redstone, boats and minecarts

Redstone

Pulse

A redstone pulse releases the shutter 2 ticks later.

Boats

Sneak + use

Place a stand in a boat by sneaking and using the item on it.

Minecarts

Auto pickup

Minecarts pick up a stand when near it.

How it works

The stand has an owner, the first player who placed or used it, who gets the advancements. A player must be nearby because the stand cannot render by itself. If the owner is out of range it uses the closest player in range (configurable). A photo taken through another player shows their view, which can differ with resource packs or shaders.
Wiki / Mods / Lightroom

Lightroom

The Lightroom prints Photographs from Developed Film. Every print needs paper and dyes, and the block needs light level 12 or higher above it.

Tap to zoom

Automation

Pulse

Prints a frame

A redstone pulse prints the selected frame, then selects the next one.

Last frame

Film ejects

After the last frame the film pops out the front. Block the front with an opaque block to prevent this.

Chromatic process

Place Tinted Glass on top of the Lightroom to make it Refracted and unlock the chromatic process. Toggle it with the button on the left. It prints one color channel at a time onto a Chromatic Sheet. Use that sheet as paper for the other channels. The last channel (blue) turns it into a normal Photograph.
ChannelDyes needed
RedMagenta + Yellow
GreenCyan + Yellow
BlueCyan + Magenta

Channels always print in order red, green, blue. Frames taken with an R/G/B filter show their channel in the tooltip.

Wiki / World / Skull Cavern

Skull Cavern

The Skull Cavern is a mining dimension that soft-resets every day. Unlock the Skull Cavern Teleporter by completing the Vault Bundle in the Community Center section of the quest book.

Reset Every dayLayers 4 plus the surfaceAccess Skull Cavern Teleporter
Descend

Ropes

You land on a bare surface. The shell is unbreakable skull stone, so the only way down is ropes hidden under boulders and ores.

Regeneration

Daily

The cavern generates once per world. Mined ores, crystals and boulders are replaced by an invisible block that regenerates slowly, so some ropes may be exposed early the next day.

Blocks

Other blocks

Other blocks regrow a few seconds after mining, with a few exceptions, so some can be farmed. Placed blocks stay overnight unless hardmode is on, so mark ropes with torches.

Surface. Nothing lives here apart from Pale Oak logs and Glow Shrooms.

Layers and biomes

Each layer has two biomes. Except for the last layer, both share the same ore pool, while mobs, structures and surrounding blocks differ.

Wiki / Artisan / Fish Pond

Fish Pond

A Fish Pond is an artisan machine that cultivates fish, roe and extra drops unique to each fish. Each pond holds one fish type.

Tap to zoom

Layout of the Fish Pond with all blocks accounted for.

Set the type

Right-click a fish

Right-click the pond with a fish to set its type. The initial population is set to 0 and the fish is consumed.

Population

Starts at 3

Fish are born each morning if the pond is not at max. Shift-click with an empty hand to take them out.

Reset

Fishing rod

An empty pond can be cleared of its type with any tier of Fishing Rod.

Moving

Keeps progress

A broken pond keeps its fish type and quest progress. It does not burn in lava.

Construction

Water

3x4 area

Needs a 3x4 area of water or lava behind it, depending on the fish. The nub side must face away from the water.

Spacing

No competing ponds

Ponds cannot sit next to or directly across from each other. Stacking vertically is fine, so high-efficiency setups stack them.

Error

Red exclamation mark

Shown above the pond when its water requirements fail.

Population quests

Every morning at 6am the population grows by 1 if it is below max. At max there is a 75% chance of a quest (yellow exclamation mark). Right-click the pond to hand in the items and permanently raise the max population, up to 10.

Produce

Daily

Roe plus extras

Each pond makes roe of its fish plus one or more items unique to that fish. Collect when the green exclamation mark shows, or automate it with a Fish Pond Basket.

Roe amount

rnd(pop / 4, pop / 2 + bonuses)

Bonuses come from the skills of the player collecting.

Extra items

Independent rolls

Each item rolls on its own, so you can get every item. Sea Biscuit and Scum Collector multiply the chance. Any chance above 25% is guaranteed.

Full quest and drop spreadsheetSunlit Valley wiki page
Wiki / Artisan / Prize Machine

Prize Machine

The Prize Machine gives set prizes at random when you give it a Prize Ticket. Right-click it to get a hint about the next prize.

Ticket

100 XP in every skill

Submitting a Prize Ticket gives 100 skill experience in every category.

Counter

Resets at the end

Each prize raises an internal counter. After the last prize is claimed it resets to 8.

Book

Frog's Bounty Bazaar

Doubles the amount of each prize. It does not add an extra roll.
